prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: מערכת שעות כיתת י'2 – סמסטר א' (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "ראשון" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שני" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שלישי" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "יום" · longest unbreakable word 36px · one-line width 36px
  col 2: header "שעה" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 78px
  col 3: header "מקצוע" · longest unbreakable word 56px · one-line width 56px
  col 4: header "מורה" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 60px
  col 5: header "חדר" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 67px
  col 6: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 619px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 629px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 628px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"poor","why":"The notes column is starved (~105px) while the day column is hugely over-wide; notes wrap into 6–8 lines and rows become very tall, with wasted white space in hour/teacher/subject."},"B":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Well proportioned: notes receives the surplus (~165px), the day column is compact, and hour, teacher, subject and room stay on one line; rows scan cleanly."},"C":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Near-ideal balance: room column sits at its one-line width, notes gets ~155px, day ~85px; all critical identifiers stay intact and only notes wrap naturally."},"D":{"grade":"bad","why":"Notes is over-allocated (~200px) while hour, teacher and room fall below one-line widths; times split at the dash, names wrap, and rooms such as 'מעבדה 1' break across lines, disrupting scanning."},"E":{"grade":"good","why":"Close to C: compact day column, adequate room, notes ~155px; critical fields stay readable, though notes gets slightly less width and the room column looks tighter than in C."}},"best":["B","C"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"Exact pixel widths are estimated from the renders; B vs C is very close, and I am not fully certain whether E's room column causes 'אולם ספורט' to wrap."}
